Convert BNF codes to AMR package antimicrobial codes

Source: R/crosswalk.R
bnf_to_ab.Rd

Maps BNF codes to the antimicrobial agent they contain. Codes longer than 9 characters (products and presentations, such as the 15-character codes in prescribing data) are truncated to the chemical substance. Codes shorter than 9 characters (chapter, section, paragraph, subparagraph) are expanded to every crosswalk chemical they contain, so bnf_to_ab("050112") lists all quinolones.

Usage

bnf_to_ab(code, output = c("table", "ab"))

Arguments

code

Character vector of BNF codes (any level).

output

"table" (default) or "ab" for a character vector of unique AMR codes.

Value

A data frame with input, bnf_chemical_code, bnf_name, ab, ab_name, atc, ab_group (one row per input and chemical), or a character vector of AMR codes. Codes not in the crosswalk give a row with NA and a warning.

See also

ab_to_bnf()

Examples

bnf_to_ab(c("0501013B0", "0501013B0AAAAAA"))   # chemical, then a 15-char presentation
#>             input bnf_chemical_code    bnf_name  ab     ab_name     atc
#> 1       0501013B0         0501013B0 Amoxicillin AMX Amoxicillin J01CA04
#> 2 0501013B0AAAAAA         0501013B0 Amoxicillin AMX Amoxicillin J01CA04
#>           ab_group
#> 1 Aminopenicillins
#> 2 Aminopenicillins
bnf_to_ab("050112", output = "ab")               # all quinolones in BNF paragraph 5.1.12
#> [1] "CIP" "OFX" "NOR" "LVX" "MFX"
